objectClass.notes: Agent visually inspected the original single architectural reference. Campus is the target extracted from a wider bay landscape; background skyline, bridge, water and neighboring forest are contextual scenery.

reasoning: A connected silver roof sweeps over multiple irregular offset landscaped courtyard voids; the surface bridges narrow connecting sections between the voids.
The near-left entrance is covered by a broad timber-lined arch with a small elliptical opening through its soffit; the right frontage forms a second broad glazed arch.
Roof edges become low at outer tips and rise substantially above entrances; mid-campus glazed edges follow the changing surface height.
Courtyard openings vary in length, angle and shape; this is not a regular array of independent donut roofs.

resolvedAssumptions: Nominal campus scale is 112 by 84 metres, maximum architecture elevation 16 metres; reference supplies no measured dimensions.
Coordinate convention: Y up, X across the campus, foreground public entrance at positive Z.
Hidden back elevations, foundations and interiors are authored architectural inference with lower confidence.
Model fidelity concerns the campus only, excluding distant geographical scenery.
Procedural PBR finish is explicitly authorized by the accepted plan; no exact photo-derived texture or inverse-rendering claim.

definitionOfDone: Civic Dune retains each identity system: One connected undulating roof surface; Multiple irregular offset courtyard openings; Actual open entrance oculus; Broad entrance arches and narrow connectors; Low outer roof edges with fitted glazing.
All visible roof shells are indexed closed meshes with distinct top, underside and fascia regions; openings remain genuine voids.
Finite geometry, consistent winding and thickness, metre-scaled UVs, fitted glazing and no unintended intersections survive seven professionally lit review viewpoints.
Stable named assemblies expose selection and exploded inspection using identical part boundaries; GLBs reimport at metre scale with self-contained textures.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

referencePbrExtraction.limitation: Accepted plan explicitly calls for independent procedural textures. Reference is one perspective-lit concept rendering; genuine de-lit independent PBR maps cannot be recovered from those pixels. Palette and material families are visual observations; channel values and microscopic texture are authored inference, not extraction results.

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold
reference lighting copied without separating material readability

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

lightingFromPhoto: Directional warm-neutral sunlight from elevated front-left; model a key around [65,95,75] and verify against the source crop shadow direction.
Cool sky fill plus an environment map provides broad metal highlights and glass reflections; interiors have restrained warm local light.
ACES filmic tone mapping and exposure near 1.0, tuned to avoid white metal clipping; pale neutral background; contact shadows ground walls and planting.

Use the same scene lighting for app and export, with 2048 pixel interactive shadows and 4096 pixel final capture shadows. Dusk shifts key intensity and activates warm rooms without blowing out glazing.
proceduralStrategy: Preserve buildDemoModel(id), Three.js/React Three Fiber integration, fixed catalog and existing persistence/Film interfaces.
Keep authored geometry data, reusable indexed-shell helpers and deterministic independent PBR generation separate.
Expose stable assembly IDs, entrance landmarks, measured bounds and rest transforms; exploded layout scales offsets around campus center.
Create watertight roof shells and fitted facades; attach seams/soffits/trim to parent assemblies.
Inspect reference hero then reverse, east, west, aerial, entrance-detail and dusk hero before acceptance.
animationAnchors: root pivot node supports whole-object translation, rotation, scale, and visibility changes
component pivot groups support later local transforms without rebuilding geometry

component seams and sockets define plausible break points instead of random explosions
risks: Single-view reference permits a coherent architectural interpretation, not exact geometry or measured material properties.

referenceAssessment.basis: Clearly identifiable campus extracted from wider scenery; adequate visible shape and palette for a reference-faithful architectural interpretation, not photogrammetry.
visibleEvidence: A connected silver roof sweeps over multiple irregular offset landscaped courtyard voids; the surface bridges narrow connecting sections between the voids.
The near-left entrance is covered by a broad timber-lined arch with a small elliptical opening through its soffit; the right frontage forms a second broad glazed arch.
Roof edges become low at outer tips and rise substantially above entrances; mid-campus glazed edges follow the changing surface height.
Courtyard openings vary in length, angle and shape; this is not a regular array of independent donut roofs.
criticalIdentityFeatures: Broad entrance arches and narrow connectors
Low outer roof edges with fitted glazing
referenceAssessment.materialFinishPolicy: Independently authored procedural base-color, roughness and normal maps; source pixels guide palette only because oblique low-resolution lit surfaces cannot supply measured reflectance or de-lit texture.
